name: German
script: Latin alphabet with ä, ö, ü and ß
region: Germany, Austria, Switzerland, Liechtenstein and parts of Belgium, Luxembourg and Italy
about: German is the most widely spoken native language in the European Union, and Germany is a top destination for Indian students thanks to its low-cost public universities. All German nouns start with a capital letter, which makes them easy to spot.
pronunciation: W is said like the English V, so Wasser sounds like vasser.
Ch after a, o or u is a throaty sound like the kh in Hindi khana, as in Buch.
Ei sounds like the English word eye, while ie sounds like ee, so mein is mine and Bier is beer.
Ü is said by rounding your lips for oo while saying ee, and Ö by rounding them for o while saying e.

lessons.intro: Hallo! Let's begin with German greetings. Germans value politeness and clear communication, so these few words will make a great first impression.
lessons.tip: Greetings change by region. In southern Germany and Austria you will hear Grüß Gott, and in the north people often say Moin. Guten Tag works everywhere.

phrases.note: Guten Tag means good day and is the polite hello. With friends or younger people, simply say hallo.
Wie geht es Ihnen is the polite way to ask how someone is. With friends, say wie geht's. Germans usually expect an honest answer.
Mir geht es gut, danke means I am fine, thanks. Casually, you can shorten it to gut, danke.
Danke means thank you. For extra warmth, say danke schön or vielen Dank, which means many thanks.
Entschuldigung works for both sorry and excuse me, for example to get past someone. For a heartfelt apology, say es tut mir leid.
Auf Wiedersehen is the polite goodbye and means until we see again. Tschüss is the friendly, everyday bye. Bis später means see you later.

lessons.intro: Now let's introduce ourselves in German. These sentences are perfect for your first day at a German university, office or language class.
lessons.tip: German has a formal you, Sie, and an informal you, du. Use Sie with strangers, officials and colleagues until they offer du. Among students, du is normal.

phrases.note: Ich heiße Priya means I am called Priya. You can also say mein Name ist Priya, which sounds a little more formal.
Wie heißen Sie is the polite way to ask someone's name. With a friend or a child, say wie heißt du.
Woher kommen Sie means where do you come from. The informal version is woher kommst du.
Ich komme aus Indien means I come from India. You could also say ich bin Inderin, meaning I am Indian, said by a woman. A man says Inder.
Freut mich means pleased to meet you, literally it pleases me. Germans often say it with a firm handshake.
Ich spreche ein bisschen Deutsch means I speak a little German. Note that sp at the start of a word sounds like shp.

lessons.intro: Let's count in German! Numbers are useful for prices, addresses and train platforms, and German trains love their timetables.
lessons.tip: German says numbers like twenty-one backwards, as one-and-twenty, einundzwanzig. Also, halb drei means half past two, literally half to three.

phrases.note: Eins, zwei, drei, vier, fünf. These are one to five. On the phone, people often say zwo instead of zwei to avoid confusing it with drei.
Sechs, sieben, acht, neun, zehn. These are six to ten. The Z in zehn is pronounced like ts.
Wie spät ist es literally means how late is it, and it is the usual way to ask the time. You may also hear wie viel Uhr ist es.
Heute means today. The eu sounds like oy, as in the English word boy.
Morgen means tomorrow. Bis morgen means see you tomorrow. With a capital letter, der Morgen means the morning.
Gestern means yesterday. The day before yesterday is vorgestern.

lessons.intro: Hungry? Let's learn how to shop and eat out in German, from bakeries to beer gardens and Christmas markets.
lessons.tip: In German restaurants you usually pay at the table, and the waiter may ask zusammen oder getrennt, together or separately. Round up or tip about ten percent.

phrases.note: Was kostet das means what does this cost. It is the simple, polite way to ask a price.
Das ist zu teuer means that is too expensive. Prices in German shops are fixed, so save bargaining for flea markets.
Ein Wasser, bitte means a water, please. You will be asked mit oder ohne, with or without gas. Say stilles Wasser for still water.
Ich bin Vegetarierin means I am vegetarian, said by a woman. A man says Vegetarier. Vegetarian food is easy to find in Germany.
Das ist sehr lecker means this is very tasty. Lecker is an everyday word. In a fancier place, say das schmeckt sehr gut.
Die Rechnung, bitte means the bill, please. You can also say ich möchte bitte zahlen, which means I would like to pay.

lessons.intro: Let's travel! Germany has a fantastic rail network, so these phrases will help you find stations, platforms and your way around town.
lessons.tip: The main station in any German city is called der Hauptbahnhof, often shortened to Hbf on signs. It is usually right in the city centre.

phrases.note: Wo ist der Bahnhof means where is the train station. For the main station, ask wo ist der Hauptbahnhof.
Biegen Sie links ab means turn left, in the polite form. People giving directions often simply say links, meaning left.
Biegen Sie rechts ab means turn right. Rechts means right, so listen for that key word.
Gehen Sie geradeaus means go straight ahead. Often you will just hear immer geradeaus, meaning keep going straight.
Wie weit ist es means how far is it. Germans may answer in minutes on foot, zu Fuß.
Können Sie mir bitte helfen means could you please help me. In an emergency, just shout Hilfe, which means help.

lessons.intro: Our final lesson! These phrases will keep any conversation flowing, even when the German gets fast. Let's wrap it up together.
lessons.tip: Bitte is a magic word in German. It means please, you're welcome, and pardon when you didn't hear something. Use it often.

phrases.note: Ja means yes and nein means no. To say yes to a negative question, Germans use doch.
Ich verstehe das nicht means I don't understand that. You can also just say ich verstehe nicht.
Sprechen Sie bitte langsamer means please speak more slowly. It is polite, and people are usually happy to help.
Was bedeutet das means what does this mean. Point at a word on a menu or sign and ask it.
Das gefällt mir means I like it, literally it pleases me. For food, say das schmeckt mir instead.
Gute Nacht means good night, said before going to sleep. When leaving in the evening, say schönen Abend, meaning have a nice evening.
